newsitem.title: CHINA: China trumpets success of prison labour.
newsitem.headline: China trumpets success of prison labour.

text.p: China on Wednesday trumpeted the use of prison labour in the southern city of Guangzhou, saying it had reduced the number of repeat offenders.
The official Legal Daily said the use of prison labour at Guangzhou Penitentiary since 1992 had reduced the rate of recidivism among ex-convicts to less than four percent.
A prison official, contacted by telephone, said the rate of recidivism at other prisons was six percent. The prisoners made garments for the domestic market, he said.
Prisoners worked an average eight hours a day and earned 70-100 yuan ($8-$12) a month, the official said. He declined to give further details.
The newspaper said 40 percent of inmates at the prison worked for pay and that the programme would be expanded to cover all inmates within two years.
Allegations of forced prison labour, sometimes involving political prisoners, have dogged China as it seeks a broader world role for its fast-growing economy.
Washington bans imports of products made by prisoners, arguing that such imports subject the United States to unfair economic competition.
